newsitem.title: FINLAND: No date yet for Finnish cen back act to parliament.
newsitem.headline: No date yet for Finnish cen back act to parliament.

text.p: No date has yet been fixed for a parliamentary debate on a proposed change in Finnish law to make the central bank independent of political influence, a government source said on Thursday.

Finnish radio earlier said the government had agreed to revise the law in line with requirements for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU). Before it goes to parliament the proposal is due for routine presidential approval on Friday.
"Parliament reconvenes in the first week of February and until then no specific dates will be known," the source said. @

Finnish radio said the proposal would strip the Bank of Finland's board of parliamentary supervisors of its authority in foreign exchange decision-making, and grant the board of management full powers over exchange rate policy.
The supervisors -- nine MPs appointed by parliamentary groups in proportion to party representation in the single-chamber legislature -- have repeatedly said they oppose such a transfer of powers.
"We feel it could be dangerous to let go of all political control over our own currency," one has said. @
But in joining the European Union in 1995, Finland effectively agreed to surrender political influence over the central bank.
